summary: Anupam Chakraborty works in Indology and other fields. He earned a Bachelor of Business Administration from Bengal School of Technology and Management (2019–2022) and a Master of Business Administration from the Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur (2023–2025).

Anuradha Seneviratna (1938–2009) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Peradeniya from around 1964 to 1968 and later served there as a professor from circa 1976 to 2003.

Anushka Kahandagamage is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an MA from the University of Colombo, an MPhil from South Asian University, and a PhD from the University of Otago, before becoming a postdoctoral fellow at Harvard University (2025–2026).

Anvita Abbi (born 1949) specializes in linguistics and Indology. She studied at Cornell University from circa 1971 to 1975 and served on the editorial board at Jawaharlal Nehru University from around 1976 to 2013.
Aparajita Kundu is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. She completed her PhD at Jadavpur University and serves as an assistant professor at Surendranath College.

Aram Frenkian (1898–1964) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Alexandru Ioan Cuza University, the University of Bucharest (PhD 1931), and under Meillet, Bloch, Finot, and Bréhier. He was Professor of Greek at Chernivtsi University and the University of Bucharest.

Archana Venkatesan is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied at De Anza College (~1993–1995) and UC Berkeley (~1995–2004), and around 2007 was appointed Associate Professor of Religious Studies and Comparative Literature at UC Davis.

Archibald Campbell (1805–1874) worked in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Glasgow, the University of Edinburgh (Dr.med. ~1823–1827), and the University of Cambridge, later serving as Lecturer in Indian Law at Cambridge and Pembroke College.

Archibald Campbell Carlleyle (1831–1897) worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He served as curator at the Riddell Museum and as an assistant to Cunningham at the Archaeological Survey of India from 1871 to 1885.

Archibald Edward Gough (1845–1915) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Oxford. He served as Anglo-Sanskrit Professor at Benares Sanskrit College, Professor of Philosophy at Presidency University, and Principal of Aliah University and the University of Allahabad.

Archie John Bahm (1907–1996) was a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Albion College and the University of Michigan, he taught at Texas Tech and the University of Denver, and was Acting Chair at the University of New Mexico.

Arend Willem Mauritz Odé (1887–1951) was a linguist who studied at Leiden University under C.C. Uhlenbeck and at the University of Copenhagen under Holger Pedersen. In 1917, he became a teacher, and later conrector in 1930, at Grotius College.
Arghyadip Mondal works in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and Indology. He has been affiliated with Ghent University as a PhD researcher attested in 2026.

Ariana Maki works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. After completing her PhD at Ohio State University in 2012, she held posts at the University of Idaho, the University of Colorado Boulder, and the University of Virginia.

Ariane Macdonald is a Tibetologist who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein and succeeded Marcelle Lalou. She taught Amy Heller and Yoshiro Imaeda, and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 1972).
Arild Engelsen Ruud specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the London School of Economics (1991–1995) and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 2007.

Arindam Chakrabarti, an Indology and philosophy scholar, earned a DPhil at Oxford. He has held positions as professor at the University of Delhi, professor emeritus at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and chaired professor at Stony Brook University.
Arindam Mondal is a scholar in Indology. He completed an M.Phil. at Jadavpur University and serves as an assistant professor at Shishuram Das College.

Arinde L. Jonker specializes in Indology and religious studies. She completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), where she studied with Daniele Cuneo and Jonathan A. Silk, and was supervised by Peter C. Bisschop.
Arion Roşu (1924–2007) studied at the University of Bucharest from circa 1942 to 1947, and later at the University of Paris under Jean Filliozat from circa 1965 to 1974.
